html:
SMTO-EXE-0244 — SMTO couldn't accept the details of this Docker request

GUID: 22d0eb4e-a814-55b2-8eb9-c0dfb106061c
Slug: docker-invalid-request
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • Some details in the Docker request were missing, in the wrong form, or not allowed, so SMTO rejected it before Docker made any change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. When asking about folders on the Gateway computer, give the full path, such as /home/alex/myapp, not a short or relative one like ./myapp. Docker builds and folder mounts only accept full paths, and the Dockerfile must be inside the build folder.
  2. Use the exact container or image name as it appears in SMTO's lists, and when publishing an image use a name with a tag such as myapp:1.0. SMTO publishes images by tag, and needs exact names so it acts on the right item.
  3. Ask SMTO to try the request again with these corrections. Nothing ran, so it is safe to try again once the details are fixed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts the request and the Docker action runs on the Gateway.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the request you typed, to the person who manages SMTO. Sending the exact same request again will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Docker request failed validation: wrong Gateway node, unknown operation or fields outside its schema, a name in both env and secret_env, both output streams disabled, relative or missing mount/build paths, a Dockerfile outside the context, an invalid cache ID, a push by digest, an update with no changes, or an oversized request.

What this means

  • Typed admission rejected operation/node/schema, overlapping public/private environment names, invalid output-channel selection, mount/build paths, cache identity or unsupported push-by-digest arguments. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Typed admission rejected operation/node/schema, overlapping public/private environment names, invalid output-channel selection, mount/build paths, cache identity or unsupported push-by-digest arguments.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific typed fields and target identity without substituting arbitrary CLI flags.

How to fix it

  • Read the rejected arguments in the activity receipt and correct them against the tool's advertised schema: use absolute Gateway paths for context_path and bind mounts, keep the Dockerfile inside the context, avoid duplicate env/secret_env keys, push by tag rather than @digest, and confirm the request targets the selected Gateway node.
  • Correct the specific typed field, path or identity error using the advertised Docker schema.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended request validates under normal scope, credential and authorization checks.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
